title: Optimal multiclass regret versus Littlestone dimension
formal: Determine \(R(d,T)=\sup\){\(R_{T}(H): H\) is a nonempty multiclass hypothesis class with \(\mathrm{L}(H)\le d\)}, up to universal constant factors, for integers \(T\ge d\ge 1\). The supremum ranges over arbitrary instance and label sets, including infinite label sets. \(R_{T}(H)\) is the full-label online minimax regret defined below; learners have no computational-efficiency restriction.
context:
The labels need not be consistent with any \(h\in H\). The learner is charged only for its excess expected mistakes over the best one fixed hypothesis chosen after the whole sequence is known.

The 2023 paper proves sublinear regret for every finite-Littlestone-dimension multiclass class, even with infinitely many labels. The remaining question is the sharp rate, not whether such classes are learnable at all.

The source gives O(\(\surd\)(dT log(eT/d))) regret, compared with the known \(\Omega (\sqrt{dT})\) lower bound. Writing \(\Theta (dT)\) would lose the square root and describe a fundamentally different claim.

For finite Y the source also obtains \(O(\sqrt{dT \log |Y|})\). This yields the desired rate when |Y| is a fixed constant, but its hidden coefficient grows with the label count. The conjecture asks for a numerical constant independent of that count.

The original conjecture predicts \(R(d,T)=\Theta (\sqrt{dT})\); the source gives a universal lower bound at that scale and an upper bound with an extra square-root logarithm in T. Determining the full minimax function permits a different answer if the conjecture fails. No equivalence to the proposed sharp bound is asserted.
why: Would determine whether Littlestone dimension alone controls the exact minimax cost of multiclass sequential prediction, beyond the already known learnability characterization.
status_note: The original game, dimension, horizon range and both upper bounds were checked. Later-result searches, the source’s arXiv version record and the May 2026 oracle-efficiency paper were checked through 12 September 2026. The latter explicitly studies binary classification; no resolution of the universal multiclass constant was located.

progress.text: The source proves label-independent regret within a square-root logarithmic factor of the lower bound and asks to remove that factor.
For finite label spaces, the same paper removes the horizon logarithm at the cost of a log|Y| factor under the square root.

sentences: An online learner predicts a label and then sees the correct label on each round.
Regret compares its cumulative prediction loss with the best hypothesis in a known class.
Littlestone dimension measures which labeled binary trees that class can realize.
The target is the worst minimax regret among all classes of dimension at most d over T rounds, with no bound on the label-space size.
Determining the full tradeoff would settle whether the familiar square-root dT scale needs an extra factor in the multiclass setting.

definitions: Let X be an instance set, Y a label set and \(\varnothing \ne H\subseteq Y^{X} a\) known hypothesis class. On round t an adversary presents \(x_{t}\in X\), the learner chooses a probability distribution \(p_{t}\) on Y, and the adversary then reveals \(y_{t}\in Y\). The learner suffers loss \(1- p_{t}(y_{t})\), the probability of a wrong randomized prediction. It observes the actual label, not just whether its prediction was correct. Its regret is \(\sum_{t=1}^{T}(1- p_{t}(y_{t}))- \min _{h\in H}\sum_{t=1}^{T}1[h(x_{t})\ne y_{t}]\). Let \(R_{T}(H)\) be the infimum over learner strategies of the supremum of this regret over adversarial plays; the adversary may observe \(p_{t}\) before choosing \(y_{t}\). This distribution-valued convention already accounts for prediction randomness. There is no computational-efficiency restriction on a strategy, and it may know T. A depth-d Littlestone tree is a complete binary tree with an instance \(x\in X\) at each internal node and two distinct labels from Y on its two outgoing edges. It is shattered by H if every root-to-leaf path has some \(h\in H\) whose labels on the encountered instances equal all the path’s edge labels. The Littlestone dimension \(\mathrm{L}(H)\) is the greatest shattered depth, or infinity if depths are unbounded. Define \(R(d,T)\) by the supremum in the statement; the bound sought is uniform across all choices of X,Y,H. If \(\mathrm{L}(H)=0\) all hypotheses agree pointwise and zero regret is attainable. The domain \(T\ge d\) avoids the separate saturation regime in which regret is capped by T.
answer_criterion: Give a positive function \(g(d,T)\) and constants \(a,A>0\) independent of both parameters, all label sets and all hypothesis classes, and prove a \(g(d,T)\le R(d,T)\le A g(d,T)\) for every integer \(T\ge d\ge 1\). Lower bounds may use families of classes; a worst-case class need not attain the supremum. This is an asymptotic regret target with multiplicative constants, not additive 0.01 error.
